The clearinghouse is append-only, fill-only, with no production delete, so a column not added before the first genome load becomes a corpus-wide backfill.

In domains/kbase/berdl/clearinghouse_schema.py, extend _CONTENT_TYPE_HEAD -- the existing per-entity-type mechanism -- adding ONLY INTRINSIC metrics (a column belongs here if two independent implementations reading the same bytes must agree on its value):
  genome: ADD gc_content DOUBLE, contig_n50 INT, max_contig_length BIGINT, min_contig_length BIGINT, n_ambiguous_bases BIGINT, assembly_level STRING. KEEP the existing fasta_reference, taxon_id, assembly_accession, n_contigs, total_length, is_closed.
  protein: ADD md5 STRING ONLY. There is NO is_fragment: PRD round 3 removed it, because start/stop completeness is a property of a feature OCCURRENCE (genome_feature.partial), not of a shared sequence. KEEP sequence, seq_length.
  gene: ADD md5 STRING, gc_content DOUBLE. KEEP sequence, seq_length, protein_entity_hash.
  function and ontology_term: DO NOT TOUCH. They are the ONLY tables with rows, so they are the only place a change is expensive, and nothing here needs it. ADD A TEST asserting their heads are unchanged -- 'extend the content heads' is exactly the instruction someone tidy applies uniformly to all five types.

DO NOT ADD completeness, contamination, coding_density OR ANY CheckM2 ASSESSMENT HERE. Those are a model's assessment, meaningless without the tool version and the model used, and they go to genome_result in the sibling task. That split is PRD Q3 and it is the decision most likely to be revisited -- implement it as written and do not 'improve' it by moving quality into content.

assembly_level IS DERIVED and its rule must be PINNED in this module as a documented function (rule below), not computed ad hoc by the loader. Values: 'complete'|'scaffold'|'contig'|NULL. KBDL (gc2-3) computes the STORED values; this function is the documented reference and must agree with KBDL on the same golden vectors. It is deliberately materialized so every consumer does not re-derive it differently; it is NOT authoritative against NCBI, whose value reflects submitter intent rather than the bytes, and the docstring must say so.

ALSO STRENGTHEN THE BOOTSTRAP VERIFICATION, because this change creates a live hazard: a deployment that bootstrapped the clearinghouse earlier has the OLD column list, and the existing adapter refuses on a PARTITIONING mismatch but says nothing about a MISSING COLUMN -- so a stale deployment would accept writes and silently drop the new fields. Make the verification compare the FULL COLUMN LIST and report a missing or extra column as an error naming the table and the column.

Preserve every existing module invariant: config values must contain NO PARENTHESIS (the guard against a partition transform leaking into a config); the DDL path emits no NOT NULL anywhere; table_configs() returns a fresh list per call; partition_by is ABSENT rather than falsy for unpartitioned tables.

TESTS: the new columns appear in the emitted schema_sql for the right three types and nowhere else; function and ontology_term heads are byte-identical to before; assembly_level's pinned rule matches every golden vector below; table_configs() still returns 21 configs (the five alias configs byte-identical to the base commit) with a fresh list per call; and the strengthened verification errors on a simulated live table missing a new column.

NORMATIVE DERIVATION RULES (identical in KBDL and KBUtilLib; both test against the SAME golden vectors), over canonicalized, upper-cased contigs:
  assembly_level: is_closed TRUE -> 'complete'; is_closed FALSE and any contig has a run of >= 10 consecutive 'N' -> 'scaffold'; is_closed FALSE otherwise -> 'contig'; is_closed NULL -> NULL. 'chromosome' is NEVER emitted (it needs submitter knowledge).
  gc_content: (count G + count C) / (count A + C + G + T) as a DOUBLE in [0,1]; ambiguity codes excluded from numerator AND denominator; denominator 0 (empty or all-ambiguous) -> NULL.
  n_ambiguous_bases: count of every base that is not A, C, G or T.
  contig_n50: sort contig lengths descending; the length of the first contig at which the running sum reaches >= 50% of total_length; no interpolation, no rounding; no contigs -> NULL.
  max_contig_length / min_contig_length: over non-empty contigs; none -> NULL.
  gene gc_content: the same rule over the gene DNA. md5: lowercase hex MD5 of the upper-cased stored sequence.
  GOLDEN CASES the tests must include: is_closed NULL; a 10-N run vs a 9-N run; an all-ambiguous contig; an empty assembly; an N50 where the running sum lands EXACTLY on 50%.

ADD ONE GENOME-ONLY ALIAS SOURCE, kbdl_genome_id, to _GENOME_ONLY_ALIAS_SOURCES with pattern ^\S{1,128}$ (non-empty, no whitespace, at most 128 chars -- KBDL genome_id values are 'G1234', bare accessions or 'unk'+ordinal, so nothing narrower is safe). Document it as STORE-SCOPED and NOT invertible: the same string means different genomes in different KBDL stores, so it must only ever be written together with the request's store_id. Do NOT add it to any invertible-sources set.

MIGRATE THE EXISTING LIVE TABLES. genome_content, gene_content and protein_content already exist in the live lake, EMPTY, in the OLD shape, so CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS would silently keep them unextended. Extend the clearinghouse bootstrap so that, for each of those three tables when it exists: (1) re-check COUNT(*) = 0 in the same run and REFUSE if it is not; (2) ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS with exactly the missing declared columns; (3) compare the FULL live column list (SHOW CREATE TABLE) against table_configs() and refuse on ANY difference. NEVER drop or recreate a table. If ALTER is unsupported (gc2-1 records it), stop and report. Every write path takes its target namespace as an ARGUMENT, defaulting to CLEARINGHOUSE_NAMESPACE, so tests and the rehearsal can use a scratch namespace.

Complete the companion: the consensus and curation tables, the request and ledger, and the two declaration logs.

1. feature_consensus(build_id, feature_id, function_entity_hash, verdict, n_tools, n_agree, agreement, rule_id, rule_version, <tail>). Per-occurrence because the INPUTS are per-occurrence (which tools ran on this build) even though each tool's call is per-sequence. rule_id AND rule_version ARE MANDATORY. DO NOT INVENT THE CONSENSUS RULE -- make it PLUGGABLE and VERSIONED, resolved by rule_id, and ship ONE reference rule clearly labelled as a reference rather than as the answer. The reason: fitness.annotation carries 272,076 rows of category/verdict/u_gene/n_hypotheses with NO record of the rule that produced them, which makes every verdict uninterpretable, and choosing the real rule is a separate decision with its own evidence.

2. feature_curation(curation_id, build_id, feature_id, assertion_type, function_entity_hash, ontology_term_entity_hash, note, asserted_by, asserted_at, supersedes_curation_id, <tail>). APPEND-ONLY with EXPLICIT supersession -- a curator's correction must never delete the evidence it corrects, both because the evidence is often still useful and because an unexplained correction is indistinguishable from a bug. assertion_type is closed to the four ASSERTION_TYPES. Supersession is per ASSERTION STREAM, a stream being (build_id, feature_id, assertion_type): supersedes_curation_id must name an existing row IN THE SAME STREAM, and the validator REJECTS a missing predecessor, a reference to another feature or another assertion type, a FORK (a second row superseding the same predecessor) and any CYCLE. Provide a resolver returning ONE effective head PER STREAM, so an ontology_add and a note on one feature coexist and a function_override never erases an unrelated assertion.

3. load_request(namespace, requested_by, requested_at, selector_json, genome_count_requested, <tail>) -- request_id is the tail's, and there is NO status column: provide a function deriving a request's status -- 'complete' when every table in RECEIPTED_TABLES has its terminal receipt AND every 'already_present' membership names an owning request that is itself complete; otherwise 'incomplete' -- and never store it. selector_json records WHAT WAS ASKED FOR -- a genome id list, an accession list, or a query -- so a request stays reproducible and auditable after the corpus moves underneath it. THIS IS WHAT MAKES LOADING SELECTIVE: only the genomes a request names are loaded, and a request naming a genome that does not exist FAILS with that genome named rather than silently loading a smaller set.

4. load_ledger -- EXACTLY ONE TERMINAL RECEIPT per (request_id, table_name), written ONLY AFTER reconciliation. Retry and in-progress state live OUTSIDE the lake, in the producer's durable inventory: an append-only reconciled=FALSE row would PERMANENTLY POISON its request, because append-only data cannot retract it, and an unreconciled table simply has NO receipt which already means not publishable. rows_expected IS DERIVED FROM THE REQUEST AND THE SOURCE, never from what was written -- a ledger comparing a number to itself reconciles trivially and proves nothing. Completion covers the declared inventory INCLUDING ZERO-ROW TABLES, EXCLUDES the ledger reconciling itself (recursive), and EXCLUDES independently-authored curation and disposition (a missing curator must not block archival forever). Read OPTIONAL_TABLES from the schema module: the four experimental tables have no KBDL producer, so a request carrying no fitness data reconciles at zero expected and zero written. Any unresolved shard blocks publication. rows_expected counts only the rows the request's 'written' memberships require. rows_written is an INDEPENDENT post-commit COUNT(*) over the table filtered to the request_id -- never the writer's own tally -- and shard_digests_json records a sha256 over each shard's sorted logical keys. The receipted inventory is the schema module's RECEIPTED_TABLES. Protect writes with ONE WRITER PER (namespace, schema_version) -- NOT per request digest, which would let two requests insert the same global build concurrently -- reusing council's ambiguous-commit recovery (council_archive.py:29, :748, :942): after a lost acknowledgement, re-read by FULL LOGICAL KEY before any retry (identical payload counts as written, a differing payload is a rejection), and re-read a possibly-landed receipt before attempting a second.

5. genome_build_currency and genome_disposition -- APPEND-ONLY IMMUTABLE DECLARATIONS, no mutable column. PROJECTION RULE for both: greatest declared_at per genome_entity_hash, tie-broken DETERMINISTICALLY by declaration_id; for currency, when no declaration exists, fall back to source_designated_current ONLY if EXACTLY ONE of the genome's builds carries it; zero or several means NO current build -- the genome is excluded from published_feature and reported (fail-closed). THE LOADER WRITES NO DISPOSITION DECLARATION. Absence remains UNPUBLISHED, never an implicit published -- the failure directions are asymmetric: wrongly withholding a result is visible and fixable, wrongly publishing a trial is neither.
